To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
E6 protein of HPV-16 activates the TATA box containing promoters in p53-dependent and p53-independent manner.
the HPV-16 oncoproteins E6 and E7 have different effects on cellular transcription.
HPV-16 E2 and E6 proteins transactivate viral promoters through p53-dependent and -independent pathways, and that p53 is involved in transactivation by E6 but not by E2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of transactivation by the papillomavirus E6 protein.
the molecular mechanisms underlying E6 transactivation of heterologous virus promoter.
the mechanism of transactivation by the human papillomaviruses (HPVs).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HPV-16E6 protein can transactivate the SV40 early and the RSV LTR promoters via p53-dependent and the E2 promoter via p53-independent pathways.
the HPV-16 and HPV-18 E6 proteins transactivated heterologous promoters through both p53-mediated and p53-independent pathways.
the E6 oncoproteins of high-risk HPV types, which are the etiologic agents of cervical cancer, are capable of transactivating a wide range of viral promoters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
p53 is involved in E6 transactivation of TATA-containing promoters, while p53 is not involved in E6 transcriptional activation of the adenovirus major late promoter.

HPV-16 E1 and E6 proteins are able to transactivate the HPV-16 promoter in a p53-independent and p53-dependent manner, respectively, whereas the HPV-16 L2 and E2 proteins are able to repress the HPV-16 P105 promoter in a pRb- and p53-independent manner, respectively.
the E6 protein has the ability to transactivate the viral promoters through two different mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transactivation of the HPV- 16 E6 protein by p53 is mediated by p 53- dependent and promoter-specific p 53- independent pathways.
the HPV-16E6 oncoprotein is a p53-dependent and -independent transcriptional activator of heterologous virus genes.
the HPV-16 oncoprotein E6 has a complex mechanism of action that is not limited to p53.
